scope: Pre-repair timing baseline for local tests, package checks, documentation, and representative hosted workflows. Timings are observations, not performance guarantees.

notes: The checkout is on a portable APFS volume and local wall times include filesystem and subprocess-start costs.
The system uv executable was 0.11.8 while workflows pin 0.11.29; dependency resolution was already complete and the test commands used the refreshed lock.

local_observations.failure_scope: One import-budget regression; three dependency-lock/tool-version evidence mismatches; two archived-track or publication-receipt path mismatches; one stale arXiv source archive; and one stale distributional-contract digest.
local_observations.note: This all-tests command includes benchmark, integration, and end-to-end markers; it is directly comparable to the Operational Assurance test selection but not to the focused hosted unit-test jobs.

local_observations.interpretation: Bounded work-stealing is materially faster, but eight resident workers increase memory pressure and expose one order-dependent lazy-module state failure.
local_observations.note: This command uses the same all-tests selection as the serial local observation.
The source package was built and checked in a clean temporary directory.
First run included 396 seconds of dependency precompilation.
The tox environment was recreated after an interpreter change; both Astro check and build regenerated Python/polyglot documentation.

hosted_reference.interpretation: Representative prior-main observations, not exact-head validation for this branch. Hosted unit jobs exclude benchmark, integration, and end-to-end markers and therefore are not direct peers of the local all-tests observations; Operational Assurance uses the all-tests selection with coverage.

findings.summary: The serial local suite takes more than 55 minutes while bounded work-stealing reduces wall time by 83%, but the current suite is not fully order-independent under xdist.
findings.required_disposition: Repair the parallel-only lazy-module failure, identify serial-only groups, benchmark bounded worker counts, and retain a non-sharded full release gate.

findings.summary: Hosted CI repeats full-suite coverage across three Python versions, a separate coverage job, and Operational Assurance.
findings.required_disposition: Use one authoritative coverage lane, focused compatibility lanes, deterministic shards, and reusable evidence while preserving full release validation.

findings.summary: The repository harness spends minutes scanning the entire checkout, including generated and vendored trees, instead of the tracked-file set.
findings.required_disposition: Run conflict-marker checks over Git-tracked text files or a reviewed exclusion set and prove identical finding behavior.

findings.summary: Fresh Python subprocesses repeatedly pay the top-level import regression, dominating wheel-consumer, CLI, Arrow, and platform-reconciliation tests.
findings.required_disposition: Restore lazy imports, consolidate safe subprocess probes, and cache build artifacts without sharing mutable test state.

findings.summary: The docs lane recreates a large tox environment and repeats polyglot extraction/build work across Astro check and build.
findings.required_disposition: Key caches by interpreter and lock, build the extractor once, reuse generated API artifacts, and retain link/type/build checks.

findings.summary: Julia first-run precompilation is expensive and warm Aqua checks dominate binding test time; Rust has a large cold-to-warm build delta.
findings.required_disposition: Cache Julia depots and Rust targets safely, split fast numerical smoke from package-quality assurance, and keep full Aqua and workspace checks in required pre-release lanes.

findings.summary: The R check glob can include stale tracked source archives and checked version 0.1.0 instead of only the newly built 2.1.0 package.
findings.required_disposition: Remove stale archives from source control and bind checks to the exact versioned artifact emitted by the current build.
